    text=page.extract_text()

(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts)[:36000])

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from itertools import product
# Two-node chain u -> v, two pipeline stages, one strategy per node.
P=((0,1),(1,0))
feasible=[]
for z in product((0,1),repeat=4):
    Z=(z[:2],z[2:])
    valid=all(Z[v][i]>=P[v][i] for v in range(2) for i in range(2))
    valid &= all(Z[1][i]<=Z[0][i] for i in range(2))
    valid &= all(Z[1][i]<=P[1][i]-P[0][i]+1 for i in range(2))
    if valid: feasible.append(Z)
print({'P_u':P[0],'P_v':P[1],'feasible_Z':feasible,'equation_4_multiplier':P[0][0]*P[1][1]})
print('Both placement sums are one and both stages are nonempty.')
PY"

strengths: UniAP addresses a useful systems problem with direct relevance to training large vision models. Jointly selecting pipeline placement and per-layer DP, TP, and FSDP strategies is a meaningful approach, and Appendix F illustrates how the resulting strategy adapts to communication topology and memory limits.

Table 1 reports substantial practical gains. On ENVB-8, ViT-Huge reaches 45.58 samples/s versus 38.74 for Alpa and 32.20 for Galvatron; Swin-Huge improves from 13.90 to 19.08 samples/s over Galvatron. The reported Llama-7B gain reaches 3.80×.

Matching Galvatron's throughput on three ENVA models while reducing reported optimization time by approximately 11–17× is also valuable. Evaluation across four hardware environments, including scaling to 64 DCUs, provides meaningful evidence of practical applicability.

The manuscript clearly organizes profiling, cost modeling, optimization, and execution. The appendices provide model configurations, solver settings, and a timing-model evaluation reporting 3.59% average relative error on selected strategies.
weaknesses: The decisive concern is a correctness gap in the stated optimization. Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity but do not order pipeline stages. For a two-layer chain u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies the placement and contiguity constraints, yet Equation (4) charges zero communication because it counts only edges from stage j to j+1. Edges skipping stages are likewise unaccounted for. Consequently, the formulation can optimize incorrectly costed pipelines; Appendix A's contiguity proof does not resolve this.

The claimed memory-feasibility guarantee is insufficiently specified. Algorithm 1 passes micro-batch size b=B/c to CostModeling, and Section 3.2 scales activation memory by this batch size. Without checkpointing, GPipe retains activations from all c micro-batches before backward execution. The manuscript does not show how this accumulation enters M or Equation (5), and provides no peak-memory validation establishing that its feasibility predictions are reliable.

The optimality and complexity claims exceed the evidence. Appendix D specifies a 60-second solver limit and early termination with an optimality gap below 4%, but reports neither achieved gaps nor timeout frequencies. These are reasonable engineering choices, yet they do not establish exact optimality. Section 3.5's polynomial runtime expression relies on treating solver time as a constant cap; it is not a complexity bound for obtaining an optimal solution.

The advertised MIQP is not supplied in solver-ready form: Equations (3) and (4) contain fourth-degree products of placement and strategy variables, such as Pui Pvi Suk Svl. Auxiliary-variable reformulations are possible, making this potentially correctable, but none is described. Together with the absence of an implementation link and incomplete strategy-dictionary construction details, this materially limits reproducibility.

The experiments do not isolate the central claim that joint optimization improves over hierarchical optimization. Figure 6 compares against inter-layer-only and intra-layer-only variants, whereas the relevant baselines support both categories. Hierarchical optimization is not inherently suboptimal, and no formal search-space inclusion or controlled comparison using the same costs and candidate strategies establishes the claimed advantage. The reported difference in cost-model accuracy is another possible explanation for better selections.

The optimization-time results require narrower interpretation. UniAP times UOP rather than the complete profiling-to-execution process, and Section 4.2 attributes substantial gains to multithreaded Gurobi versus single-threaded baselines without reporting a controlled thread comparison. The DCU comparison also contrasts modeled search with execution-based enumeration. These remain useful wall-clock observations, but do not establish the claimed algorithmic advantage. The formulation gaps and missing attribution evidence collectively favor Weak Reject despite the worthwhile empirical results.
